title: Chopin, Nocturne Op. 15 No. 2, in five recordings
work: Nocturne in F♯ major, Op. 15 No. 2
question: How much does the quiet, fast middle section change the melody when it returns?
intro: The F♯-major melody is heavily ornamented, and the middle section is faster. Chopin marked it doppio movimento, twice the motion, and asked for the opening of that passage to be played sotto voce. Paderewski’s recordings, made twenty years apart, are listed here alongside those of Liszt’s pupil d’Albert and the younger pianists Faulkner and Prati.

recordings.label: Eugen d’Albert, 1916
recordings.note: Kempff recalled that d’Albert could make a single A♯ tremble like a human voice.

recordings.label: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, 1917
recordings.note: In his Victor recordings Paderewski often spread chords and let the two hands enter at different moments.

recordings.label: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, 1937
recordings.note: The pianist who defended stolen time returned to the nocturne twenty years after his New York recording.

recordings.label: Luke Faulkner
recordings.note: Faulkner studied piano and composition at Chetham’s, then trained in music for the screen at Edinburgh.

recordings.label: Patrizia Prati, 2015
recordings.note: A pupil of Aldo Ciccolini and András Schiff, Prati recorded this nocturne at Madrid’s Museum of Romanticism.

passages.label: Opening melody
passages.note: The right hand plays small flourishes around a sustained melody, and evenly spaced bass notes and chords sit beneath the phrase.

passages.label: F♯-minor phrase, dolcissimo
passages.note: The F♯-minor phrase falls from its high notes, its little runs marked dolcissimo — very sweetly.

passages.label: Middle section, dotted melody
passages.note: A dotted tune sits above quick notes in the same hand. The bass leaps beneath it. The opening is quiet.

passages.label: Climax of the middle section
passages.note: The dotted rhythm continues, the piano grows louder and the middle section reaches its climax.

passages.label: Pause before the opening returns
passages.note: The repeated figure slows and dies away. After a pause the opening melody returns.
